      <title>Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/ebola-swiss-patient-nigeria-dr-congo-concerns-virus-spread</link>
      <description><p>Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda</p><p>Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.</p><p>The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/ebola-swiss-patient-nigeria-dr-congo-concerns-virus-spread">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’</p></li><li><p>Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record</p></li></ul><p>Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/13/f1-returns-to-africa-for-first-time-since-1993-with-10-year-rwanda-deal-from-early-2030s">set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s</a>. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.</p><p>Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">immigration</a> jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.</p><p>Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)</a> facilities in south Florida.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines</title><description>Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 03:20:31 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Americas</category><title>Trump says US may launch ‘another little Epic Fury’ attack on Iran</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261023-trump-says-us-may-launch-another-little-epic-fury-attack-iran</link><description>
US President Donald Trump on Friday said his country may launch “another little Epic Fury” on Iran, referring to the joint Israeli-American military operation that sparked the war with Iran at the end of February.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f8bb93a2-cf20-11f1-9296-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26296694621760.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f8bb93a2-cf20-11f1-9296-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26296694621760.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5ed26606-cf22-11f1-b95a-b30ab0d5f083</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 20:50:51 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f8bb93a2-cf20-11f1-9296-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26296694621760.jpg">© Mark Schiefelbein, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Eye on Africa</category><title>Building collapse in Nairobi search for survivors under way</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/building-collapse-in-nairobi-search-for-survivors-under-way</link><description>
In tonight's programme, scramble to get through rubble to trapped survivors after a more than 10 storeys building being built in Nairobi goes down.  Also, Kenya says that there's been a second Ebola death. Earlier this week it had logged 9 cases so far, all traced back to its first Ebola patient who died earlier this month. And in finally the 11th edition of the iconic contemporary art festival Also known as Africa taking place in Paris, we speak to Cape Verde's artist Amadeo Carvalho.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6ca47780-cf20-11f1-a61d-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bed663fa.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6ca47780-cf20-11f1-a61d-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-bed663fa.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1750ef52-cf20-11f1-996d-211c1872ac14</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 20:31:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Georja CALVIN-SMITH</dc:creator></item><item><category>The World This Week</category><title><![CDATA[After French Riots, Curfews & Calm .. is a new Storm Brewing ? Plus Ukraine & Israel]]></title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/the-world-this-week/20261023-after-french-riots-curfews-calm-is-a-new-storm-brewing-plus-ukraine-israel</link><description>
It's been a week that’s seen mass protests hijacked by violent rioters across France. The looting of shops, trashing of public buildings, the burning of Lyon’s Tourist Information and the iconic Limoges City Hall.  After the riots, came the curfews, and the contemplation, who did what and why weren’t they stopped. Seditious groups, ultra left anarchists and opportunist criminals said President Macron, with a qualified mea culpa: failures in anticipation and authorities dropped the ball in intelligence gathering. Macron is out of breath,  exhausted and disorientated claimed the Presidential Frontrunner Marine Le Pen, the far right leader now polling in an even stronger position for the Presidency. Foreign leaders had a free for all too, President Trump wading in and Israel’s prime minister settled old scores ahead of elections there. But France wasn’t isolated in its protests and unrest, Milan was a mirror image, with demonstrations in Spain, Portugal, Belgium too, An Autumn of Discontent, and more protests to follow this weekend:
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d79f6d6a-cf11-11f1-ade7-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/%C3%89meute-urbaine-et-rencontre-diplomatique.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d79f6d6a-cf11-11f1-ade7-4b25c96ec90e/w:1024/p:16x9/%C3%89meute-urbaine-et-rencontre-diplomatique.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8347fab2-cf10-11f1-8b03-fd96aae311a0</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 18:48:11 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Netanyahu weighs West Bank operation ahead of elections: ‘Politically, it will not help anybody’</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261023-netanyahu-weighs-west-bank-operation-ahead-of-elections-politically-it-will-not-help-anybody</link><description>
As Israel approaches a consequential parliamentary election amid renewed violence in the occupied West Bank, Yedioth Ahronoth Senior Journalist Ben-Dror Yemini offers a critical assessment of Benjamin Netanyahu's political prospects, the limits of military escalation and the shifting relationship between national security and electoral legitimacy.
 
Since October 7, 2023 "Netanyahu is not popular anymore," Yemini argues, identifying the Hamas-led attacks as a decisive turning point in the Israeli prime minister's public standing.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5a830376-cf04-11f1-89ad-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261023-184343-185025-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5a830376-cf04-11f1-89ad-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261023-184343-185025-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">480ae5d2-cf0f-11f1-b644-a93470ff4a93</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 18:26:35 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Middle East</category><title>How Israeli settlers wearing keffiyehs are attacking West Bank olive groves</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261023-how-israeli-settlers-wearing-keffiyehs-are-attacking-west-bank-olive-groves</link><description>
The olive harvest officially began in the West Bank on October 15, 2026, and it has coincided with an uptick in violence towards Palestinians carried out by both Israeli settlers and soldiers. Meanwhile, the settlers and soldiers have been using social media to promote an aesthetic, Instagram-friendly and nationalistic view of these harvests.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20c2ffac-c986-11f1-8f58-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/olive-cover.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20c2ffac-c986-11f1-8f58-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/olive-cover.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f25a53be-cef7-11f1-9b67-fd117c779604</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 17:21:00 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20c2ffac-c986-11f1-8f58-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/olive-cover.png">© The Observers</source><dc:creator>Marguerite Ipek LACROIX</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Fri, 23 Oct 2026 23:26:41 +0000 en <![CDATA[ SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (photos) ]]> SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast.

The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California).

The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes.

The booster, meanwhile, reoriented for its descent back to Earth. As the mission clock passed 8 minutes, B1063 began its landing burn, and it touched down about 20 seconds later on SpaceX's droneship "Of Course I Still Love You." This was the 36th launch and landing for B1063, which notably launched NASA's DART asteroid-smashing mission in November 2021.

The Falcon 9's upper stage completed its first engine burn shortly after B1063 landed and will coast for about 45 minutes before initiating a second and final orbital insertion burn. Following that burn's execution, deployment of the vehicle's 27 satellites into LEO is scheduled to begin 62 minutes after launch.

Previous Booster B1063 launches

Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich | DART | Transporter-7 | Iridium OneWeb | SDA-0B | NROL-113 | NROL-167 | NROL-149 | NAOS | 26 Starlink missions

Today's Starlink liftoff adds to SpaceX's growing constellation of more than 11,000 active spacecraft. But Starlinks aren't launching quite as often as they used to, as SpaceX shifts its focus from the Falcon 9 to its bigger and more powerful Starship rocket.

Starship is designed for full reusability and is equipped with a payload bay outfitted to accommodate SpaceX's upgraded Version 3 Starlink satellites, which are too large for the workhorse Falcon 9. Starship is still under development, but once the rocket begins operational flights (and that day is getting closer), SpaceX plans to phase out the Falcon 9 and its Falcon Heavy variant almost entirely.

Falcon 9's 100th launch of 2026 was the Starlink 10-49 group from SpaceX's pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, which was later revealed to be the final Falcon 9 Starlink mission that would fly from Florida's Space Coast. The same might soon be true for Starlink launches from the West Coast as well.

The reduction in missions lifting off from Florida has slowed Falcon 9's Starlink launch cadence considerably. At their peak, these missions were flying every two to three days. But the most recent one before today lifted off 11 days ago, and that launch itself was the first Starlink mission in more than three weeks.

Today's launch was the 116th Falcon 9 flight so far in 2026, with about three-quarters of those being dedicated to Starlink. The reduced cadence will likely solidify 2025 as the Falcon 9's busiest year ever, with 165 launches completed. At its current rate, the Falcon 9 is expected to fly just under 150 missions by the end of this year.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA lays out plan for Artemis 3 moon-lander test flight —but when will it launch? ]]> NASA just gave us our best look yet at its Artemis III moon-lander test flight.

The agency laid out a detailed concept of operations for Artemis III today (Oct. 23) during a press conference at Kennedy Space Center, stressing how important the flight is to its moon plans and how challenging it will be to make everything go right.

"We're launching three of the most powerful rockets in the world, and undertaking what is likely the most complicated launch campaign ever undertaken," Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, said during today's event, which lasted more than two hours.

Those three rockets are NASA's Space Launch System (SLS), SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's New Glenn, all of which will fly from Florida's Space Coast.

If all goes according to plan, New Glenn will lift off first, carrying Blue Origin's Blue Moon lunar lander to low Earth orbit (LEO). SLS will go next, launching the Artemis III astronauts — NASA's Randy Bresnik, Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio, and the European Space Agency's Luca Parmitano — aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft.

SLS will deploy Orion into a highly elliptical orbit, one that gets as close to Earth as 18 miles (29 kilometers) and as far away as 1,122 miles (1,806 km), according to Parsons. The capsule will then maneuver itself into an orbit with an altitude of about 345 miles (555 km).

"That's really about getting thermal stability," Parsons said. "Orion was built as a deep-space vehicle, and so we're going to have to really manage the thermal environments, which are higher in a low Earth orbit."

The Artemis III crew will spend two days checking out Orion and its systems in LEO before meeting up with Blue Moon, which will take place on Flight Day 3 at an altitude of 273 miles (439 km).

"Over the next two days, the crew will conduct operations docked with Blue Moon," Parsons said. "They're going to open up the hatch. They're going to enter the lander. They're going to evaluate the environmental controls, the life support systems. We'll confirm that the spacecraft can maintain the right atmospheric pressure, and we're also going to test emergency scenarios, dual vehicle control, and we're going to put our Mission Control teams through their paces."

After those operations are complete — likely on Flight Day 6 or thereabouts — Starship will launch, with a specially built docking adapter on its nose.

The SpaceX vehicle — the 171-foot-tall (52 meters) upper stage of its fully reusable Starship megarocket — will meet up with Orion in LEO on Flight Day 8, at an altitude of about 237 miles (381 km). But this will be a very different encounter than the rendezvous with Blue Moon.

"The demonstration with Starship is shorter, about two hours," Parsons said. "The crew will not enter the Starship during the mission, but it gives us critical data and allows us to really understand the forces of docking, how we're going to push, how we're going to work together."

Artemis III will continue for another six to nine days after Orion undocks from Starship before finally heading back down to Earth for a parachute-aided ocean splashdown. (The nominal mission length is 14 days, Parsons said, but it could last as long as 17 days.)

During that time, the crew will evaluate their survival suits — something that didn't get done during the 10-day Artemis II flight around the moon this past April — and do a variety of other work as well, from detailed health assessments to scientific experiments and technology demonstrations. The main goal is to keep everything on track for Artemis IV, which will land astronauts near the moon's south pole in 2028, if all goes to plan.

"Everything we do on Artemis III is designed to reduce risk for our future lunar landing missions," Parsons said. "We're teaching these teams how to work together, how to make critical real-time mission decisions, all in an environment that is low Earth orbit, where if something goes wrong, we can come home much more quickly."

It's unclear at the moment which of these two privately developed landers — Blue Moon or Starship — will fly on Artemis IV, pulling off the first crewed lunar touchdown since Apollo 17 in 1972.

NASA is still preserving optionality, "to give both of our lunar landing partners the greatest opportunity for readiness in advance of astronauts landing on the moon in 2028," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said during today's event.

"We have no intention of surrendering a viable path to the surface before the data and schedule compels us to do so," he added.

No matter what decision NASA makes for Artemis IV, both Blue Moon and Starship should hit the gray dirt relatively soon, according to Parsons. "Regardless of who goes first, both providers are planning for lunar landing missions in 2028," he said.

And those missions will be quite different from each other. For example, on Blue Origin touchdowns, Orion will meet up with Blue Moon in lunar orbit. On SpaceX landings, however, Starship will likely dock with the NASA capsule in Earth orbit and propel it to the moon, Parsons said — the "push" he referred to above.

It remains unclear when exactly Artemis III will launch. NASA is targeting the summer of next year but may find it tough to meet that timeline: Last month, in an internal memo, Isaacman told agency employees that Artemis III was about 90 days behind schedule.

Some of the biggest challenges have involved the supply chain for the mission's lunar landers, Parsons said during today's event. But he and Isaacman both stressed that NASA is confident in its ability to work through such issues.

"We're moving with real speed and purpose right now," Isaacman said.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission ]]>

On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station.

The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts.

Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station, they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node.

After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module. This made room for Harmony to then dock at its permanent home next to the Destiny module.

Why it mattered

In 2007, the International Space Station was much smaller than it is today in terms of living space for its astronaut crew. The Harmony connecting module changed all that.

The STS-120 mission opened a new phase of ISS expansion by adding a vital connecting hub for future modules. Prior to Harmony's launch, the last new room addition to the ISS had occurred in 2001, when Russia's Pirs docking module (since discarded) arrived.

The Harmony module (its original name was Node 2), was the second NASA-led hub module (after the Unity, or Node 1, module) for the ISS. It was built for NASA by the Italy-based Thales Alenia Space and is covered with five "common berthing mechanisms," or connecting points for different ISS modules.

After the two-week STS-120 flight, Harmony was moved from a temporary berth at the Unity module to the forward port on the NASA's main Destiny laboratory. Once there, it served as a connection point for Europe's Columbus lab on the starboard side, and Japan's massive Kibo lab on the port side. Some of its ports have been used by visiting caargo ships and a docking port on its roof allows visiting vehicles to park there.

Inside the module are eight payload racks that include four used for avionics and four others for either stowage or crew quarters. NASA's astronaut crew quarters are based in the Harmony module. The name Harmony was selected durng a public naming contest by NASA.

]]> <![CDATA[ Halley's Comet dazzles from afar in spectacular astrophoto of Orionid meteor shower ]]>

Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity.

Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth, but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky.

McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21. Each of the shooting stars can be seen racing away from the shower's apparent point of origin — or radiant — which is located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion.

Successfully imaging a shooting star takes a combination of skill, luck and patience. McCollum photographed the meteors over the course of multiple 30-second exposures taken with a Canon EOS Ra camera and RF 28-70 f2.0 lens, which was fixed unerringly on the radiant with the aid of a star tracker. The individual exposures were then combined into a single composite image using the astrophoto software PixInsight.

Canon EOS R7 camera

The Canon EOS R7 is the best camera for beginners. Despite its crop sensor, the EOS R7 can rival most full-frame cameras. It features a 34.4MP sensor, ISO range up to 32,000 and a video capability of 4K UHD 60p. It has the best tools to help a beginner master photography. Read our full Canon EOS R7 review.

The familiar stars of Orion's Belt glisten to the right of McCollum's image, close to the glow of the Orion Nebula — one of the nearest major star forming regions to Earth. The Rosette Nebula (Caldwell 49) can also be spotted embedded in the dense starfield and dust lanes of the Milky Way's galactic plane, which runs diagonally through the composite image, as can numerous star clusters.

The Orionid meteor shower is active until Nov. 7, so be sure to head outside over the next few nights for a chance to spot one of Comet 1P/Halley's dazzling shooting stars. If you're lucky, you may even spot a Halloween Fireball belonging to the Taurid meteor shower, as Earth passes through the debris streams cast off by Comet 2P/Encke!

You can also take a look at our picks of the best lenses and cameras for astrophotography available in 2026, including the Canon EOS R8, which delivers the essential interval shooting functionality you need to capture meteors without bursting the bank.

]]> <![CDATA[ Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo? ]]> Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War.

Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise.

Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.

This year’s full remake of Combat Evolved's campaign delivered exactly what it promised: a shiny, 2026 version of the game that made audiences fall in love with the franchise. It was a clear attempt to reignite faith in 343’s vision, but how is a faithful, shinier remake proof of anything?

It might not even matter anymore, as the new Xbox leadership has rocked the ship again, leaving Master Chief and the universe’s future cloudier than ever before. Now, with rumors of a reboot being considered at new steward Activision, is there hope for the Spartans, or will Xbox run into another dead end?

Rebooted or not, Halo needs to leave Master Chief behind

It looks like the ‘Halo Studios’ moniker only lasted a single (remade) game, as Xbox has recently announced that Call of Duty maker and publisher Activision — which houses many FPS-oriented studios — is taking over development, essentially leaving the 343 veterans as a minor support studio, which translates into more layoffs.

If we put aside the human and institutional cost of this whole back-and-forth over the years (a big ask in today’s climate), there are reasons to be optimistic about the quality of an Activision-developed Halo. Regardless of what you think about the Call of Duty IP in 2026 and the publisher’s overall vision for it, it’s clear there’s plenty of talent holding everything together and, more importantly, enough experience to iterate on what Halo’s multiplayer side needs to shine bright again.

But this won’t fix the larger issue with Halo, which is that Master Chief should’ve been left behind long ago. Like it or not, it’s difficult to deny Halo’s “golden era” ended with Halo: Reach (Bungie’s swansong under Xbox) and the Halo Wars spinoffs, which took the series into the real-time strategy genre. These games were wildly different, but they had one core thing in common: they made the sci-fi setting feel bigger instead of smaller, offering the perfect blueprint to build upon in a post-Halo 3 world.

There’s nothing inherently wrong with the Master Chief. Franchises can be built around iconic characters like Mario or Lara Croft. But in the post-Bungie era, his role changed from an extremely competent Spartan soldier to a space messiah. Halo 4, 5, and Infinite used sci-fi nonsense to transform him into this larger-than-life figure, rendering the rest of the UNSC largely powerless in the process.

It’s the same mistake ID Software made with Doomguy, centering the story on how super special he is, and not on the world he inhabits. Now rumours are rumbling that Activision’s reboot might focus on Chief’s origins; that's the last thing Halo needs.

Are Halo 2 and 3 remakes happening?

Forgetting Activision’s next Halo for a second, we were teased with (even if there wasn’t an official confirmation from Xbox) at least a Halo 2 remake via Halo: Campaign Evolved’s alternative ending.

Back in May 2026, renowned insider Rebs Gaming confidently reported that Halo 2 and 3 remakes were in development. But can fans realistically expect them after new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s latest shakeup?

Halo Studios could have done a "fine" job with safe remakes of the two original Halo sequels while Activision handles new projects. It’s hard to reject that approach, especially after Xbox finding success with Bethesda’s The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered and confirming two Fallout remasters are in the works. It seems like money waiting to be made, but the remakes could be cooked too.

Xbox and 343/Halo Studios have made plenty of mistakes with Halo, but the killer has always been their lack of conviction in their ideas. And look, nostalgia shouldn’t be the driving force behind a franchise in dire need of reinvention, but I’m far more annoyed by the creative rollbacks, flip-flopping, and now the loss of knowledge and talent accompanying the gutting of Halo Studios.

Xbox Live Action

We haven’t even touched on the mess that was the live-action Halo show. It lasted only two seasons, had John-117 walking around outside the Mjolnir armor for most of its runtime, and was cancelled just as the story finally got to the titular Halo. Why would you stray so far from the source material, and how do you miss the mark so badly?

In many ways, it perfectly encapsulated what’s been wrong with Halo as a whole for so many years. The powers that be can’t decide what they really want from it, and thus it’s stuck, unable to leave the past behind or convincingly establish a new horizon for itself. Other franchises have run into the same issues — looking at you, Star Wars — but Halo has been stuck in this purgatory for 15+ years, as Xbox leaders and strategy shifts come and go.

Could Xbox’s newly-formed XP division deliver the focused big-screen adaptation the series has always deserved? I’m sure that’s the plan, but even a cursory glance back at Xbox’s handling of the franchise for the past decade or so says no.

Halo’s deep problems won’t be fixed overnight, and throwing a bunch of hard-working developers to the curb certainly won’t help. Halo’s current struggles didn’t come from Halo Studios or 343 Industries; they came from impatient and incompetent leadership calling the property-defining shots. I’ve seen nothing to suggest that’s changed.

]]> <![CDATA[ Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026 ]]>

The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year.

What is it?

At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. The spacecraft was put through environmental testing that explored how the vehicle will fare in the extreme conditions it will experience on its ride to the surface of the moon.

This testing simulated the extreme temperatures, shaking and even the sounds that the spacecraft will experience from launch to landing. And, as JPL announced recently, the lander passed this series of tests with flying colors, as we can see in this image snapped Aug. 31 of the lander inside the 25-foot-wide (7.6 meters) space simulator at JPL.

"NASA JPL’s Environmental Test Laboratory has been putting robotic explorers to the test since the Ranger program gave us NASA’s first up-close views of the moon's surface in the mid-1960s. We’re proud to provide our expertise and facilities to support this new phase of commercial lunar exploration," Charles Whetsel, manager for the Exploration Systems Development Office at JPL, said in a statement.

Why is it incredible?

Griffin-1 is expected to launch to the moon later this year as part of NASA's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative. The spacecraft will carry over 1,100 pounds (455 kilograms) of cargo to its landing site near the lunar south pole.

In this cargo will be science experiments and new technologies that will be tested on the moon's surface, including Astrolab's FLIP rover, which will explore the lunar surface with a history-making supercomputer onboard.

This suite of experimental hardware won't just expand our understanding of the moon up close. Griffin-1's exploration will also help set the stage for a future, crewed moon base, which NASA aims to build near the south pole over the next half-decade or so.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds ]]> Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.

For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter, whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe.

Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

In the new study, researchers investigated whether dark matter could be made of "stupendously large black holes," ones with masses greater than 100 billion times the mass of the sun. Stupendously large black holes greater than 1 million billion to 10 million billion suns in mass would be heavier than entire galaxies.

So far, astronomers have not detected any stupendously large black holes — currently, the largest black hole known may weigh about 36 billion suns. Since researchers have not seen any even after looking at many galaxies, the new study noted they cannot make up all of dark matter — but team members wondered if the exotic objects still might constitute a significant portion of the puzzling substance.

Often, dark matter is thought of "as a fine dust spread everywhere," study co-author Christopher Gerlach, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics in Germany, told Space.com. However, if dark matter is packed into a handful of gigantic objects such as stupendously large black holes, "the universe becomes grainy on very large scales. And we can check that."

Specifically, the scientists analyzed the light from the dawn of the universe, study co-author Yann Gouttenoire, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics, told Space.com.

For the first 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the cosmos was filled with a hot plasma in which light was trapped. Eventually, the expansion of the universe let the cosmos cool enough for the plasma to largely dissipate and form atoms. This in turn let light shine freely, "and that light is still arriving today," Gerlach explained. "We call it the cosmic microwave background, a snapshot of the infant universe covering the whole sky."

The temperature of the cosmic microwave background "varies from place to place by about one part in 100,000," study co-author Antonio Iovino, a theoretical physicist at New York University, Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, told Space.com. "That pattern tells us how matter was spread back then."

Analyzing the cosmic microwave background revealed it is not grainy the way stupendously black holes would have made it. "So these black holes can't be a significant part of the dark matter," Nicholas Leister, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics, told Space.com.

The researchers cautioned that the new findings do not suggest that stupendously large black holes cannot exist, only that they do not make up a major fraction of dark matter. Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.

For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter, whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe.

Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

In the new study, researchers investigated whether dark matter could be made of "stupendously large black holes," ones with masses greater than 100 billion times the mass of the sun. Stupendously large black holes greater than 1 million billion to 10 million billion suns in mass would be heavier than entire galaxies.

So far, astronomers have not detected any stupendously large black holes — currently, the largest black hole known may weigh about 36 billion suns. Since researchers have not seen any even after looking at many galaxies, the new study noted they cannot make up all of dark matter — but team members wondered if the exotic objects still might constitute a significant portion of the puzzling substance.

Specifically, the scientists analyzed the light from the dawn of the universe, study co-author Yann Gouttenoire, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics, told Space.com.

For the first 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the cosmos was filled with a hot plasma in which light was trapped. Eventually, the expansion of the universe let the cosmos cool enough for the plasma to largely dissipate and form atoms. This in turn let light shine freely, "and that light is still arriving today," Gerlach explained. "We call it the cosmic microwave background, a snapshot of the infant universe covering the whole sky."

The temperature of the cosmic microwave background "varies from place to place by about one part in 100,000," study co-author Antonio Iovino, a theoretical physicist at New York University, Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, told Space.com. "That pattern tells us how matter was spread back then."

HawkEye 360 provides this data to the U.S. government and its allies "to enable faster, better decision-making," according to the company. "Our space-based collection, proprietary signal processing and AI-powered analytics transform knowledge of the RF spectrum into a strategic advantage."

HawkEye 360's first satellites launched in 2018, and the company has now sent nearly 50 of them to LEO. The most recent Hawk launch before "We're Not Hawking Around" came just two days ago; three of the satellites went up on SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission.

"We're Not Hawking Around "was Rocket Lab's 98th launch to date and its 19th of 2026 so far. Sixteen of this year's flights have been performed by the two-stage, 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron. The other three have been conducted by HASTE, a suborbital variant of Electron that allows customers to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment.

]]> <![CDATA[ Space debris: Are we on track for true sustainability? (op-ed) ]]> David Zamora is the chairman of the Space Data Association. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights.

The commercialization of space is well underway, and as a result, Earth’s orbit is becoming ever more congested. The current number of active satellites in orbit stands at around 16,000, according to the European Space Agency( ESA), and this number is expected to jump close to 60,000 by 2035, Novaspace projects. While it’s not always given the recognition it deserves, space has fast become a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. Therefore, it’s critical that a safe and clean operating landscape is maintained.

Yet this is becoming increasingly challenging, particularly given that, alongside the rapid increase in space traffic, there are also more than 1.2 million pieces of debris over 1 centimeter (0.4 inches) cm in Earth’s orbit, each of which could damage satellites and spacecraft and potentially cause disastrous consequences. With the number of active satellites and debris objects in space continuing to increase, the space environment is under growing pressure.

Balancing expansion with sustainability

Space was once the sole domain of nation states, but this is no longer the case. As technology has advanced, launch costs have decreased, and satellites have become more efficient, smaller and cheaper to build. These changes have democratized space, resulting in a massive increase in space traffic, not least constellations in low Earth orbit (LEO) that comprise thousands of satellites.

Plans are underway to further expand these constellations, and new and even bigger constellations are also expected to launch in the coming years. Added to that, we’re also likely to see the first space-based data centers within the next few years, which may well mark the start of the wholesale shift of data centers from Earth to space, which will further add to the congestion already being felt.

To ensure that space continues to meet our current and future needs, this continued expansion must happen in a sustainable way. Maintaining a safe and clean landscape is more important than ever before, and mitigating the impact of space debris is critical to that effort.

Maintaining a safe environment

Mitigating the impact of debris involves a multipronged approach. Whether intentional or unintentional, the creation of new space debris by future space missions must be minimized as much as possible. This applies during launch, operation, and end of life phases, and satellites and other spacecraft need to be designed with this in mind. Additionally, satellites that are no longer active should not remain in orbit for extended periods, because this only increases the chance of collision events which would create new debris. The standard rule has been 25 years, but there are recommendations now that this should be lowered to five years.

Also critical is the prevention of in-orbit collisions between active satellites and other objects. This is only achievable through effective Space Situational Awareness (SSA) and Space Traffic Coordination (STC) systems. SSA maps out and characterizes objects in space (both satellites and debris), determining their location, trajectory and velocity, while STC actively manages the space traffic identified through SSA to prevent collisions. When a conjunction is probable, SSA/STC service providers alert the operators involved, who then decide whether to undertake a collision-avoidance maneuver.

Extending the operational life of satellites is another important aspect of debris mitigation because it reduces the need for so many new launches, thereby reducing the likelihood of more debris being created. Innovations such as electric propulsion systems that allow for greater maneuverability and extended mission durations are part of the solution, as is in-orbit servicing, maintenance and refuelling.

While these strategies focus on preventing new debris from being created, we also need effective methods for removing existing pieces of debris. This is a rapidly growing sector attracting much investment. Debris-removal technology being developed ranges from physical capture and tethered deorbit to destruction with ground and space-based laser ablation and plasma systems, as well as the emerging concept of mining debris to extract metals and gases for in-orbit processing to feed into the circular space economy.

How stakeholders are responding

The UN views space safety and space sustainability as urgent priorities. Its treaties and agreements focus on preserving the peaceful, safe, and sustainable use of outer space, preventing collisions, managing space debris, and ensuring responsible operations. Governments, space agencies and international organizations are also strengthening their focus on space sustainability.

ESA has launched its Zero Debris strategy, which is aimed at achieving a debris-neutral orbital environment by 2030. As part of this approach, ESA has updated its debris mitigation requirements and standards that will govern how its missions are designed, built, flown and disposed of. It also sets requirements for any company or institution that works with ESA on its missions.

In the U.K., the UK Space Agency is also taking a proactive role in space safety and sustainability through its Active Debris Removal (ADR) program and through the development of space sustainability standards in partnership with industry. It is also in the process of developing a space sustainability strategy to ensure a coordinated approach to sustainable practices in space.

On the other side of the pond, NASA’s Space Sustainability Strategy identifies five key challenges that are felt nationally but also within the wider space community. These include the absence of a single framework for space sustainability that has been accepted by the space community and the fact that space sustainability may be in tension with other mission interests. The strategy defines six goals that are intended to address each of the challenges alongside corresponding objectives to guide NASA’s achievements of the goals.

The U.S. is also building on the National Orbital Debris Mitigation Plan, which was released in 2022, with the Orbital Sustainability (ORBITS) Act. The Act, which has been introduced to the Senate but not yet been enacted into law, seeks to establish a program for the active remediation of orbital debris as well as requiring the development of uniform orbital debris standard practices. The Office of Space Commerce has also developed TraCSS (Traffic Coordination System for Space) to provide basic SSA data and services to civil and private space operators in support of spaceflight safety, although the system is currently in beta mode.

The International Standard Organisation (ISO) is also working on a standard for STC (Space Traffic Coordination) so that SSA activities can be standardized. Titled Space Systems — Space Traffic Coordination (STC), the standard is moving toward final publication, and its core focus is on establishing baseline protocols, data exchange formats and operational requirements for space safety, on-orbit conjunction assessment and collision avoidance.

Beyond today

While these strategies are certainly moving the industry in the right direction, there is a real need to act quickly. Success will rely not only on speed, but also on sustained and collaborative effort, as well as engagement from all space users. The decisions made and actions undertaken over the next decade will shape the space environment for generations to come.

As to whether sustainability becomes a core principle rather than an afterthought, that remains to be seen. There is, however, reason to be optimistic.

]]> <![CDATA[ Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test ]]> Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for.

The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model, from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

"Following several successful tests using representative vehicle masses, the latest system-level drop test in October was not completed as planned due to an anomaly during the parafoil deployment sequence," an ESA spokesperson confirmed in an email to Space.com. "An independent investigation is ongoing to determine its root cause and inform the next steps."

Space Rider is being developed as Europe's first reusable orbital spacecraft — an uncrewed vehicle designed to carry scientific experiments to orbit for up to two months, then return them to Earth for analysis. Its method of return, though, differs from that of any other spacecraft in operation today. Space Rider''s wingless, lifting-body design relies on a steerable parachute, or parafoil, to maneuver toward its landing area. This allows it to perform runway-style touchdowns, as opposed to other, less accurate parachute-aided recoveries in current practice.

This month's drop test was intended to demonstrate that ability, which is a critical requirement for Space Rider's planned reuse after missions in orbit, but the impact of its failure may not end up disrupting its ultimate development timeline. According to Géraldine Naja, ESA's director of space transportation, the vehicle's other remaining qualification tests aren't holding back its path to launch.

"We hope that this test will not damage, or let's say lead us to modify, the remaining schedule and qualification activities," Naja said during an ESA Council media briefing on Oct. 22. "In any case, the remaining qualification activities are not on the critical path of the development of the Space Rider."

Naja described the incident as an unfortunate but important event. "We have had many successful tests before, but testing and validation is part of the development of a space system," she said.

The lost vehicle was a full-scale test model assembled to evaluate Space Rider's descent and landing systems. The minivan-sized mockup reproduced the size and flight characteristics of its reentry module, with avionics to control its autonomous guidance and navigation systems, but the vehicle was far from a space-ready article.

The Oct. 6 test took place at a military range on the Italian island of Sardinia, where the mockup was released from a helicopter at an altitude of approximately 2 miles (3 kilometers). According to Naja, the vehicle's initial drogue parachute triggered as expected and began slowing the Space Rider mock-up's descent before its larger, steerable parafoil was supposed to unfurl. The parafoil, however, detached during deployment, leaving the vehicle in freefall before impacting the ground. ESA has subsequently recovered all the craft's components.

This month's event was the first drop test since an unsuccessful attempt in May, when a sensor flagged an issue during preparations, prompting engineers to abort the test before the model was released. Following that, Space Rider's testing range, operated by Italy's Ministry of Defense, was unavailable from June through September.

Space Rider's descent and landing qualification campaign began in 2025, with previous successes demonstrating its parafoil deployment and autonomous capabilities. Beyond its landing systems, Space Rider also underwent separate thermal protection testing earlier this year, exposing its heat-shield materials to temperatures around 2,900 degrees Fahrenheit (1,600 degrees Celsius) in plasma wind tunnel trials.

ESA has targeted Space Rider's first orbital mission for later this decade.

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/pripad-podvodnice-dnes-je-ceska-obec-sokolska-uplne-jinou-organizaci-rika_2610240010_jho</link>
 <description>Česká obec sokolská si příští týden připomene vznik Československa tradičním během republiky. V jaké kondici je organizace po nepříjemném případu defraudace, který už několik let vyšetřuje policie? „Od té kauzy jsme digitalizovali celou řadu agend, které brání tomu, aby někdo padělal dokumenty. Máme u všech oběhů dokumentů digitální auditní stopy, takže je vše jasně dohledatelné,“ říká pro Radiožurnál starosta České obce sokolské Martin Chlumský.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Politolog: V obecních volbách se chovají lidé jinak, než u sněmovních. Vládní strany na to dojíždí</title>

 <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) označil neúspěch kandidátů svého hnutí ve druhém kole senátních voleb za katastrofu a ohlásil restart. Jeho součástí má být přijímání nových členů a hledání osobností pro příští volby do horní komory parlamentu. „Největší překvapení voleb byl určitě ne příliš veselý výsledek hnutí ANO,“ míní politolog Jakub Čapek v Osobnosti Plus.</description>

<item>
 <title>Zrušení poplatků je cesta k zestátnění médií veřejné služby, říká Šebelová. Nerušil: Systém je zastaralý</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/zruseni-poplatku-je-cesta-k-zestatneni-medii-verejne-sluzby-rika-sebelova_2610232233_jos</link>
 <description>Vládní koalice prosadila v pátek nečekaně do programu Sněmovny projednání vládního návrhu na zrušení televizního a rozhlasového poplatku. „Dnes koncesionářský poplatek využívá zhruba třetina zemí Evropské unie. Myslím, že tady je i správný argument, že chceme jít s dobou, chceme jít se Západem,“ říká poslanec za SPD Josef Nerušil. „Je to reakce na prohrané volby,“ nesouhlasí předsedkyně poslaneckého klubu STAN Michaela Šebelová.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/_zuj3734_260113-153202_zuj.jpg?itok=lRsWIRPT" type="image/jpeg" />

<item>
 <title>Válka očima četníka i německé dělnice. Severočeské muzeum chystá expozici o sudetském Liberci</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/valka-ocima-cetnika-i-nemecke-delnice-severoceske-muzeum-chysta-expozici-o_2610231806_brz</link>
 <description>Severočeské muzeum v Liberci chce využít suterénní prostory pro netradiční expozici o říšské župě Sudety. Ta byla za 2. světové války součástí fašistického Německa a Liberec byl jejím hlavním městem. Do stavebních úprav suterénu už se muzeum pustilo. Na vytvoření samotné expozice ale spolu s Libereckým krajem hledá finance. Má ukázat 2. světovou válku z pohledu zdejšího regionu a přiblížit, jaký vliv měla na jednotlivé skupiny obyvatelstva.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Po změně času hrozí cyklistům i chodcům další pokuty. Neznají pravidla</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/doprava/zmena-casu-nova-pravidla-pro-cyklisty-i-chodce-hrozi-pokuty/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=doprava</link>
   <description>V noci ze soboty 24. října na neděli 25. října se Česko vrátí k zimnímu času. Slunce tak bude zapadat o hodinu dříve, na ručičkách hodinek už před pátou odpoledne. Na silnicích se zhorší podmínky pro chodce, cyklisty i řidiče, kteří budou častěji cestovat za šera a tmy. Deník.cz se blíže podíval na povinnosti, na které upozorňuje policie. Odborníci na bezpečnost na silnicích přidávají rady, kdy reflexní prvky a funkční osvětlení zachraňují životy. Aktuální období totiž patří k nejrizikovějším v roce.</description>
   <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 05:30:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/doprava/zmena-casu-nova-pravidla-pro-cyklisty-i-chodce-hrozi-pokuty/</guid>
   <category>Doprava</category>
   <enclosure url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/fe9/fe953a58-40ff-4c33-bd45-e3d869a05257.jpeg" length="0" type="image/jpeg"/>
   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/fe9/fe953a58-40ff-4c33-bd45-e3d869a05257.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Se změnou času přichází tma dřív. Pozor na povinnosti chodců a cyklistů. Nedodržením pravidel riskují životy i pokuty.</media:description>
    <media:credit>Se svolením Adély Beranové</media:credit>
   </media:content>

   <link>https://karlovarsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/dobra-duse-petra-se-stara-o-postizeneho-syna-i-bratra/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>„Prostě se musím postarat.“ V několika slovech je možná celý příběh čtyřicetileté Petry Traganové z Toužimska. Maminky, která se po těžké životní situaci ocitla v roli člověka, na němž závisí péče o jejího syna Tomáše. Pomáhá i postiženému bratrovi. Nečeká se založenýma rukama a hledá možnosti, jak pomoci. Zkouší rehabilitace, učí syna používat elektrický vozík a raduje se z každého malého pokroku.</description>

   <title>Dětské kroužky raketově zdražily. Rodiče jsou zoufalí, obracejí se na sbírky</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/skolstvi-a-vzdelavani/cesko-skolstvi-krouzky-zdrazily-cena-kritika/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=skolstvi-a-vzdelavani</link>
   <description>Rodiče čelí ve školním roce 2026/2027 výraznému nárůstu výdajů za volnočasové kroužky. Podle statistik stouply příspěvky ve většině sportovních oddílů, přičemž výdaje rostou i za další aktivity. Stále častěji se proto rodiče obracejí s žádostmi o finanční výpomoc na sbírky a různé projekty, které jim s nouzí pomáhají. Týká se to především samoživitelů. Dobrou zprávou je, že solidarita u Čechů stoupá a přispívají v různých sbírkách.</description>

   <description>/OSOBNOST DENÍKU/ Fotbalisté Doks jsou aktuálně nejžhavějším kandidátem na vítězství v sedmé nejvyšší soutěži v Libereckém kraji. Aktuální lídr západní skupiny rozjel sezonu velmi dobře. Hodně k tomu přispívá tamní odchovanec Jakub Šimon (31), který se po dlouhých letech v létě vrátil tam, kde s fotbalem začal.</description>

   <guid>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/fotbal-kraj/doksy-maji-zpet-sveho-hazarda-kanonyra-simona-vlastni-goly-hodne-prekvapily/</guid>

   <title>Třinec poprvé v sezoně vyšel bodově naprázdno. Slaví v Českých Budějovicích</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/hokej/tipsport-extraliga-vysledky-trinec-ceske-budejovice-konec-serie-prvni-porazka/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=hokej</link>
   <description>Každá série jednou končí, stejně tak i ta třinecká. Oceláři ve 13. kole Tipsport extraligy premiérově prohráli v normální hrací době. Triumf slaví České Budějovice, které na ledě suverénního lídra soutěže vyhrály vysoko 6:2. Doma se nevedlo ani královéhradeckému Mountfieldu, který sice dotáhl proti Karlovým Varům tříbrankovou ztrátu, nakonec ale padl v prodloužení. Zbývající čtyři utkání domácí zvládli. Tři body slaví Litvínov, Vítkovice i Liberec, výhru v prodloužení pak Kladno.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Koalice protlačila v sobotu po půl páté ráno konec poplatků ČT a rozhlasu</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/koalice-prosadila-prednostni-jednani-o-konci-poplatku-pro-ct-i-rozhlas.A261023_095639_domaci_kop#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Koalice ANO, SPD a Motoristů sobě prosadila vládní návrh na  zrušení rozhlasových a televizních poplatků, zatím tedy jen v prvním čtení. Vláda chce, aby Česká televize a Český rozhlas byly financovány ze státního rozpočtu. Hlasovalo se v sobotu po půl páté ráno, což na návrh šéfa Sněmovny Tomia Okamury prosadila vládní většina.

</description>

    <item>
      <title>Desítky demonstrantů chtěly vniknout do Sněmovny. Pak letěla první kostka</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/demonstrace-malostranske-namesti-praha-poslanecka-snemovna-koncesionarske-poplatky.A261023_223701_domaci_tmps#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Na demonstraci u Poslanecké sněmovny na pražském Malostranském náměstí zasahovala v pátek večer policie. Protestující se pokusili proniknout do budovy, kde poslanci právě projednávají zrušení koncesionářských poplatků. Nikdo se nezranil, ale dění poté začalo opět eskalovat.</description>

      <media:description>Na demonstraci u Poslanecké sněmovny na pražském Malostranském náměstí zasahovala v pátek večer policie. Ženu, která hodila dlažební kostku, policisté zadrželi. (24. října 2026)</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Macinka požádá o policejní ochranu pro ministra kultury Klempíře</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/sef-motoristu-sobe-macinka-pozada-o-policejni-ochranu-pro-ministra-kultury-klempire.A261023_234726_domaci_kop#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Policejní ochranu pro ministra kultury Oto Klempíře, který předložil návrh zrušit poplatky pro Českou televizi a Český rozhlas, bude chtít šéf Motoristů sobě a ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka. „Pro pana ministra kultury požádám o přidělení policejní ochrany,“ sdělil iDNES.cz Macinka poté, co policejní těžkooděnci zasáhli proti pokusu několika desítek demonstrantů vniknout do Sněmovny.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Česko hledá zdravotníky už i v Asii. Je tu víc peněz a bezpečí, říká asistent z Filipín</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/cesko-hleda-zdravotniky-uz-i-v-asii-je-tu-vic-penez-a-bezpeci-rika-asistent-z-filipin.A261023_192014_domaci_kton#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>V Česku stále víc roste nepoměr mezi počtem zdravotníků a lidí, kteří potřebují péči. „Stárneme a vymíráme. Časem se o seniory nebude mít kdo starat. Proto lákáme zdravotníky z ciziny. Bez nich už se neobejdeme,“ říká ředitel krnovské nemocnice, lékař a senátor (ANO) Ladislav Václavec. Nedávno si vybral dvanáct budoucích zaměstnanců na Filipínách. Na další už čeká i řada jiných nemocnic.</description>
      <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 22:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci">Zprávy - Domácí</category>

      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/DAV8299401ecd_DF_FILIP2_14656509_CMYK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Nábor. Zdravotníci z Filipín se hlásí  o práci v Česku. Nemocnice je potřebují, výběrem však projde jen asi čtvrtina zájemců.</media:description>

      <description>Lidé v mnoha evropských zemích mají často hluboko do kapsy, roste nájemné, stejně tak ceny potravin a energií. Státům rostou náklady na stále dražší půjčky, takže není kde brát na chátrající školy či na dotace bydlení. Politici nemají mnoho možností, jak vyhovět sílícím protestům, které začaly ve Francii a trvají už bezmála měsíc.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Uživit se dá i z půl hektaru, dokazují jihočeští pěstitelé Tereza a Jakub Peškovi</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/domaci/zemedelstvi-peskovi-zelenina-farma.A261023_133251_ekonomika_drh#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Pár kilometrů jihozápadně od jihočeských Vodňan v ranním mlžném oparu pracuje mladý farmář. Sklízí zeleninu, stará se o květiny. Sezona nyní v polovině října pomalu končí, musí ale ještě připravit poslední bedničky pro zákazníky. Je to Jakub Pešek, který v Libějovických Svobodných Horách každý den dokazuje, že se dá uživit i bez velkých ploch.</description>
      <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 22:00:00 GMT</pubDate>

      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/103/cl6/DRH77281659b1_221857_14856192.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Tereza a Jakub Peškovi původně ze zemědělského prostředí nejsou. Nyní ale pěstují na půl hektaru zeleninu a květiny.</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Evropská směrnice zpřísní čištění odpadních vod. Česko čekají miliardové investice</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/domaci/cisteni-odpadnich-vod-evropska-smernice-srazkova-voda.A261022_141746_ekonomika_rie#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Implementace nové evropské směrnice o čištění městských odpadních vod si v České republice do roku 2045 si vyžádá podle odhadů ředitele Sdružení oboru vodovodů a kanalizací ČR (SOVAK ČR) investice ve výši 130 až 180 miliard korun. Ty však mohou mít i praktický přínos, protože mohou přispět k efektivnějšímu hospodaření s vodou. V Česku podle něj odtéká bez dalšího využití více než 90 procent dešťové vody, přestože by se dala využít.</description>
      <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 22:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/domaci">Ekonomika - Domácí</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/domaci/cisteni-odpadnich-vod-evropska-smernice-srazkova-voda.A261022_141746_ekonomika_rie/diskuse</comments>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261022_141746_ekonomika_rie</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/053/cl6/RIE90b21d214d_140105_4236488.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>V další části čistírny se od vody odděluje biologický kal. Vyčištěná voda následně pokračuje do potoka. (27. května 2026)</media:description>
      <media:credit>MAFRA</media:credit>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Lžete, přestaňte hecovat společnost a vyzývat k demonstracím, napsal Babiš</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/babis-vyzval-opozici-aby-prestala-eskalovat-situaci-a-vyzyvat-k-demonstracim.A261023_164355_domaci_aoc#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš chce, aby opozice přestala vyzývat k demonstracím a pochodům do ulic kvůli tomu, že Sněmovna začala v pátek jednat o zrušení poplatků pro Českou televizi a Český rozhlas a jejich financování ze státního rozpočtu. „Vyzývám opozici, aby přestala eskalovat situaci ve společnosti,“ napsal na sociální síti X předseda vlády a ANO.
</description>
      <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 20:51:54 GMT</pubDate>

      <description>Vedení České televize je znepokojeno překotným způsobem, jakým chce Poslanecká sněmovna projednat návrh na zrušení koncesionářských poplatků. <title>EU se snaží zmírnit nedávno zavedená obalová pravidla, která potápí malé e-shopy. Rada a Parlament se ale neshodnou, jak na to</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/eu-se-snazi-zmirnit-nedavno-zavedena-obalova-pravidla-ktera-potapi-male-e-shopy-rada-a-parlament-se-ale-neshodnou-jak-na-to/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Povinnost, která malým e-shopům komplikuje prodej do dal&#353;ích zemí EU, by se mohla pro malé e-shopy zmírnit. Evropský parlament i Rada EU chtějí pozastavit pravidlo, podle něhož musí firmy jmenovat zástupce pro roz&#353;ířenou odpovědnost výrobce v jednotlivých zemích, kam dodávají zboží v obalech. Neshodují se ale na tom, koho by se výjimka měla týkat.</description>

<item>
 <title>Studentská opozice vyráží do boje proti Vučićovi. Co čekat od předčasných parlamentních voleb v Srbsku</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/srbsko-volby-studenti-vucic_2610240700_ula</link>
 <description>V Srbsku se budou v neděli konat předčasné parlamentní volby. Dnes už bývalý prezident Aleksandar Vučić je vyhlásil na začátku září. O pár týdnů později k nim přidal i svou rezignaci. Jeho hlavním soupeřem ale letos není opozice parlamentní, nýbrž ta studentská. Podle průzkumů jsou šance vyrovnané. Studenty k volbám dovedly už téměř dva roky trvající protivládní protesty, které zahájili po tragédii na vlakovém nádraží v Novém Sadu.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-19t100028z_7_261020-230423_ula.JPG?itok=qkgBa6JF" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Sat, 24 Oct 2026 07:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Podlézat Putinovi jako Trump není na místě, vadí TOP 09. Pozlátko má v Rusku velkou roli, míní v ANO</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/podlezat-putinovi-jako-trump-neni-na-miste-vadi-top-09-pozlatko-ma-v-rusku_2610232337_jho</link>
 <description>Rusko tento týden znovu vyslalo rakety na Kyjev. Nedlouho předtím přitom dalo najevo, že v zásadě souhlasí s obnovením mírových rozhovorů. Na čí straně stojí Spojené státy? A co má dělat Evropa? „Jsem kritický na všechny strany, vidím i pokrytectví Evropské unie,“ upozorňuje europoslanec Tomáš Kubín (ANO). „Evropská diplomacie je paralyzovaná lidmi, jako je Andrej Babiš (ANO),“ kritizuje pro Český rozhlas Plus europoslanec Ondřej Kolář (TOP 09).</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/0e0b6feda40e0f333696ecadfb51a95c.png?itok=mYoy50Ki" type="image/png" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 23:37:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Mareček: Obvinění Kushnera stojí na anonymních zdrojích. Zapadá to ale do chování americké vlády</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/marecek-obvineni-kushnera-stoji-na-anonymnich-zdrojich-zapada-ale-do-chovani_2610231753_vsn</link>
 <description>Jared Kushner, zeť a velvyslanec Donalda Trumpa, popřel obvinění Vanity Fair, podle něhož nizozemská zpravodajská služba při sledování aktivit na jeho telefonu odhalila finanční transakce, do kterých byly zapojeny vlády z Blízkého východu. „Nevíme, do jaké míry hraje roli zájem USA a kdy záměr Trumpovy rodiny,“ říká pro Radiožurnál David Mareček, amerikanista z Katedry mezinárodních vztahů a evropských studií Metropolitní univerzity Praha.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-09-05t165914z_1_260906-062554_ape.JPG?itok=jHtCIgd3" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 17:53:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Netanjahu po útoku u Hebronu zvažuje největší operaci na Západním břehu od roku 1967</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/netanjahu-po-utoku-u-hebronu-zvazuje-nejvetsi-operaci-na-zapadnim-brehu-od-roku_2610231442_vsn</link>
 <description>Izraelský premiér Benjamin Netanjahu v pátek po střelbě u Hebronu prohlásil, že zvažuje na Západním břehu Jordánu největší vojenskou operaci od roku 1967. Napsala to izraelská média a agentura AFP. Podle Netanjahua je armáda připravena příkazy vykonat. Oznámení přichází několik dní před parlamentními volbami, v nichž bude šéf izraelského kabinetu usilovat o znovuzvolení.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/69580b50e98f3ff1a01622008e84f266.jpg?itok=ji63_dbo" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 14:42:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Nejméně jednoho mrtvého si vyžádala střelba na předměstí Paříže. Policie pachatele zadržela</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/nejmene-jednoho-mrtveho-si-vyzadala-strelba-na-predmesti-parize-policie_2610231245_vsn</link>
 <description>Nejméně jednoho mrtvého si v pátek dopoledne vyžádala střelba na předměstí Paříže. Informoval o tom podle agentury AFP policejní zdroj, podle něhož muž střílel na ulici. Informaci poté potvrdil i francouzský premiér Sébastien Lecornu. Další čtyři lidé utrpěli zranění. Podle úřadů jsou na místě záchranné složky a počet obětí zatím není definitivní.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-003636156_260706-165309_pik.jpg?itok=1Kq9o5hJ" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 12:45:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Poblíž břehů Rumunska se potápí zasažená loď. Nejméně jeden člověk zemřel</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-pobliz-brehu-rumunska-se-potapi-zasazena-lod-nejmene-jeden-clovek-zemrel_2610231213_vsn</link>
 <description>Rumunští záchranáři pátrají po námořnících ze zasažené nákladní lodi poblíž rumunských břehů v Černém moři. Jeden člen většinově ukrajinské posádky zemřel, tři se pohřešují, devět se podařilo zachránit, píší média s odvoláním na rumunský námořní úřad. Rumunský prezident Nicušor Dan obvinil z útoku na loď Rusko, které podle něho eskaluje válku proti Ukrajině.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-07-29t093131z_5_260826-225003_ula.JPG?itok=706U9wUQ" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 12:13:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Rakousko vyhostilo čtyři ruské diplomaty. Jeden z nich působil při OBSE, další tři na ambasádě</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/rakousko-vyhostilo-ctyri-ruske-diplomaty-jeden-z-nich-pusobil-pri-obse-dalsi-tri_2610231131_vsn</link>
 <description>Rakouské ministerstvo zahraničí v pátek oznámilo, že vyhošťuje čtyři ruské diplomaty. Dopustili se podle něho jednání, které je v rozporu s jejich diplomatickým statusem. Tři diplomaté působili na ruské ambasádě, jeden v ruské delegaci pro vojenskou bezpečnost a kontrolu zbrojení při Organizaci pro bezpečnost a spolupráci v Evropě (OBSE), informuje agentura APA. Moskva uvedla, že na rozhodnutí Vídně odpoví.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/profimedia-065366782_221025-093036_pj.jpg?itok=_Xk-qLsM" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:31:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Netanjahu v reakci na ranní střelbu nařídil blokádu Západního břehu. Pozastavil i předvolební mítinky</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/netanjahu-v-reakci-na-ranni-strelbu-naridil-blokadu-zapadniho-brehu-pozastavil-i_2610231055_vsn</link>
 <description>Izraelský premiér Benjamin Netanjahu ohlásil uzávěru okupovaného Západního břehu Jordánu kvůli střelbě z pátečního rána u města Hebron. Uvedla to agentura AFP. Blokáda by měla začít v pátek. Netanjahu také nařídil armádě okamžitě vytvořit kolem města Hebron kordon.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/cf476cfb1f01cdad5222ada3e7a07a4d.jpg?itok=b5T5Dy9S" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:55:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Vučić nebo studenti. V Srbsku skončila kampaň před volbami, reálnou šanci na vítězství mají dva subjekty</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/vucic-nebo-studenti-v-srbsku-skoncila-kampan-pred-volbami-realnou-sanci-na_2610231038_vsn</link>
 <description>Ve volbách půjde o boj dvou nejsilnějších politických formací. Roky vládnoucí koalice Sjednocené Srbsko exprezidenta Aleksandra Vučiće a opozičního hnutí s názvem Studenti vítězí. To vzešlo z dvouletých protikorupčních protestů v Bělehradě.
</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/img_3087_261023-062451_vsn.jpeg?itok=nw31070m" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:38:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>
<item>
 <title>Výraznější role pro Evropu. Pavel má patřit mezi kandidáty na vyjednavače o Ukrajině, píše britský web</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/vyraznejsi-role-pro-evropu-pavel-ma-patrit-mezi-kandidaty-na-vyjednavace-o_2610230828_vsn</link>
 <description>Prezident Petr Pavel patří mezi pět politiků, o nichž evropští lídři uvažují jako o hlavním vyjednavači s ruským vládcem Vladimirem Putinem o ukončení války na Ukrajině. Napsal to ve čtvrtek večer britský zpravodajský web The Telegraph s odvoláním na diplomatické zdroje, podle nichž už byli někteří z možných kandidátů osloveni.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-09-23t162620z_1_260923-203718_jar.JPG?itok=hgKagaMj" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:28:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>

<description>Prvním bodem dne&#353;ního jednání Poslanecké sněmovny bude zákon o zru&#353;ení televizních a rozhlasových poplatků a převedení České televize a Českého rozhlasu pod státní rozpočet. <item>
<title>Zatímco se řešily chyby v PHP, útočníci propašovali malware do oblíbené open-source knihovny</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/zatimco-se-resily-chyby-v-php-utocnici-propasovali-malware-do-oblibene-open-source-knihovny/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Během dění kolem kritické zranitelnosti v PHP se útočníci pokusili zneužít dal&#353;í roz&#353;ířený nástroj, upozorňuje kyberbezpečnostní startup Aisle, který založili Ondřej Vlček, Stanislav Fort a Jaya Ballo. Podle firmy se podařilo dostat &#353;kodlivý kód do nové verze knihovny LiteLLM pro Python, kterou vývojáři používají při práci s modely umělé inteligence a která má přes 20 milionů stažení týdně. Malware měl krást přístupové údaje a umožnit útočníkům vzdáleně spou&#353;tět vlastní příkazy. Napadení potvrdili i tvůrci Lite LLM, kteří zveřejnili také dal&#353;í podrobnosti.</description>

<author>redakce@lupa.cz (Lupa.cz: Iva Brejlová)</author>
<pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 07:23:03 GMT</pubDate>
<enclosure url="https://i.iinfo.cz/images/112/data-unik-dat-bezpecnost-kyberkriminalita.jpg" length='32024' type="image/jpeg"/>
